thesis: Frontken has genuine service growth, positive cash and a bank-debt-free funding position, but the bear carries the premium per-share-return objection. At 47.18x trailing earnings, RM80.148m receivable absorption and warrant-funded liquidity weaken the headline growth/value inference. Positive CFO growth and the constructive chart preserve an upside case, making neutral more proportionate than a funding-fragility sell.
strongest_counterexample: H1 CFO increased to RM62.623m despite receivable absorption, leaving RM35.491m FCF, and substantial liquidity supports the RM118m Taiwan program without bank borrowing.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable H1 FCF above RM35.491m with receivable cash absorption below RM80.148m and no new warrant/equity proceeds would weaken the cash-quality/dilution objection.
Comparable H1 FCF at or below zero would invalidate the positive operating-funding counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Exact quarterly-report publication date was not retrieved; fiscal periods and comparative statements are verified.
decisive_factors: Liquidity is partly financed by RM636.783m warrant proceeds, not wholly earned operating cash.
Revenue growth and positive FCF are real, but the premium requires improved per-share cash delivery.
